summary: shot gathers, ensembles 1-10, 480 traces x 200 samples @ 4 ms

notes: The textual header gives no usable CRS information. The coordinates look like a projected grid (metres or feet), but the projection, zone and datum must be supplied by the user.

decisions.label: Byte order
evidence: The binary header only makes sense read this way.

decisions.label: Samples per trace
evidence: File size divides exactly into traces of this length.

decisions.label: Sample format
evidence: IBM-normalisation test on 40,000 non-zero samples: 0.00% have a zero leading fraction digit (genuine IBM floats: 0%; IEEE floats: typically 5-10%).
This agrees with the declared format.

decisions.label: Data type
evidence: Byte 9 (FieldRecord) stays constant for runs of about 53.2 traces while byte 13 cycles within each run: the file is organised as ensembles (gathers) of ~53 traces.
The ensemble number is also stored in byte(s) 11.

decisions.label: Ensemble (gather) key
evidence: Byte 9 (FieldRecord) stays constant for runs of about 53.2 traces while byte 13 cycles within each run: the file is organised as ensembles (gathers) of ~53 traces.
The ensemble number is also stored in byte(s) 11.

decisions.label: Coordinate scalar
evidence: With scalar -100 the bin/trace spacing is 12.504 m, a standard survey size.

decisions.label: Coordinate reference system
evidence: The textual header gives no usable CRS information. The coordinates look like a projected grid (metres or feet), but the projection, zone and datum must be supplied by the user.

issues.title: Coordinate system unknown
issues.detail: The file gives no usable CRS clue. The textual header gives no usable CRS information. The coordinates look like a projected grid (metres or feet), but the projection, zone and datum must be supplied by the user.
issues.fix: Supply it with --crs EPSG:xxxx. Without it the survey can't be placed on a map with confidence.
issues.explain: The coordinates are numbers on some map grid, but nothing says which grid.
